title: 부탁 거절하기: 미안하지만 좀 어려워요
objective: By the end, you can use words like 부탁, 거절하다, 곤란하다, 어렵다, and 사정 in short sentences to turn down a request politely and give a reason.
summary: Learn ten words for asking favors and politely saying no in Korean.

task.title: Use the refusal words
task.line: Choose, fill in, put in order, or write a short answer using the words from page 1.

words.meaning: a favor (that you ask someone for)
words.example: 부탁이 하나 있는데 지금 시간 괜찮아요?
words.exampleMeaning: I have a favor to ask. Do you have a moment now?

words.meaning: to do what someone asks; to say yes to a favor
words.exampleMeaning: Thank you so much for doing me this favor.

words.meaning: to say no to (a request); to turn down
words.exampleMeaning: It was my team leader asking, so it was hard to say no.

words.meaning: to be awkward or hard to agree to (a soft way to say no)
words.example: 갑자기 돈을 빌려 달라고 하면 좀 곤란해요.
words.exampleMeaning: It puts me in a tough spot when you suddenly ask to borrow money.

words.meaning: to be hard to do (used politely to mean 'I can't')
words.example: 죄송하지만 이번 주말에는 어려울 것 같아요.
words.exampleMeaning: I'm sorry, but I don't think I can make it this weekend.

words.example: 집안 사정이 있어서 모임에 못 가요.
words.exampleMeaning: I can't come to the get-together because of a family matter.

words.meaning: to be sorry (less formal than 죄송하다; 미안해 to friends, 미안해요 to peers like coworkers)
words.exampleMeaning: Sorry, I don't have time today.

words.meaning: actually; to tell the truth (before giving the real reason)
words.exampleMeaning: Actually, I already have other plans that day.

words.example: 이번에는 안 되고 다음에 꼭 같이 가요.
words.exampleMeaning: I can't this time, but let's definitely go together next time.

words.meaning: to be a shame; to feel sorry that you missed something
words.exampleMeaning: It's a real shame I can't go with you.

exercises: Choose the word that fits each sentence: ① 너무 바빠서 선배의 부탁을 (들어줬어요 / 거절했어요). ② 마침 시간이 있어서 동료의 부탁을 (들어줬어요 / 거절했어요).
Fill in each blank with 사정, 사실은, or 다음에: ① 개인 ____이 있어서 회의에 늦었어요. ② ____ 저도 그 영화를 벌써 봤어요. ③ 오늘은 바쁘니까 ____ 만나요.

Fill in the blank with the right form of the word in brackets: ① 내일까지 다 끝내기는 좀 ____ 것 같아요. (어렵다, -(으)ㄹ) ② 생일 파티에 못 가서 정말 ____. (아쉽다, -아/어요) ③ 연락이 늦어서 ____. (미안하다, -아/어요) ④ 그 질문은 대답하기 좀 ____. (곤란하다, -아/어요)
Choose the polite refusal (a or b): 동료: "이번 토요일에 이사하는데 좀 도와줄 수 있어요?" a) 네, 몇 시까지 가면 돼요? b) 미안해요. 그날은 일이 있어서 좀 어려워요.
Put the parts in the right order to make one sentence. Start with 미안하지만: 사정이 / 미안하지만 / 좀 어려워요 / 있어서
Answer in Korean: Your friend asks, "내일 네 차 좀 빌려줄 수 있어?" Say no politely. Use 미안하다 and 곤란하다 (or 어렵다), and give a reason.
answers: ① 사정 ② 사실은 ③ 다음에
① 어려울 ② 아쉬워요 ③ 미안해요 ④ 곤란해요
Sample answer: 미안해. 내일은 내가 차를 써야 해서 좀 곤란해. (Other answers are fine if they say sorry, give a reason, and use 곤란하다 or 어렵다, e.g. 미안해. 내일은 약속이 있어서 좀 어려울 것 같아.)
